headline: Chips Lead a Broad Friday Rally as Software Sells Off; Geopolitics and Trade Shape the Week Ahead
body_html:
Markets closed out the final Friday of September on a constructive note, with 347 of 544 names in our universe finishing higher. Semiconductors were the session's clear standard-bearers, advancing 2.44% as a group and pulling the broader tape upward. Homebuilders added 1.31% and Materials rose 1.09%, while Industrials and Consumer names posted modest gains. The lone meaningful drags were Software, off 0.82%, and Energy, which slipped 0.42%.

The session's sharpest individual moves underscored the chip-sector conviction. MaxLinear surged 10.0% to top all gainers, followed by Veeco Instruments at 9.28% and Credo Technology at 7.65%. Bloom Energy climbed 8.27% in the fuel-cell space, while STAAR Surgical added 7.49%. On the other side of the ledger, Zscaler tumbled 10.06% to lead all decliners, with Twilio dropping 7.96% and Qualys and Okta both shedding more than 5%, a clear reminder that software-security names remain under pressure.

Heading into the new week, investors will be navigating a crowded geopolitical backdrop. A U.S.-China agreement on AI dialogue and tariff reductions covering some $30 billion in goods provides a measured tailwind for risk assets, though Iran-related tensions and an unsettled diplomatic calendar at the United Nations warrant close attention as quarter-end positioning takes hold.

briefs.headline: U.S. and China Forge AI Dialogue Pact, Trim Tariffs on $30B in Goods
briefs.body: Washington and Beijing agreed during a high-level summit to open a formal channel on artificial intelligence and to reduce duties on a $30 billion slice of bilateral trade. The deal emerged from the Xi visit and offers a degree of relief for technology and industrial supply chains heading into the fourth quarter.

briefs.headline: Iran Tensions Simmer After Trump Rejects Peace Overture
briefs.body: Tehran's military signalled readiness for a potential renewed confrontation with the United States even as Iranian officials continued to press for a diplomatic resolution following Washington's rejection of a peace proposal. The standoff adds a layer of uncertainty for energy markets and risk assets as the new week begins.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Equipment Names Roar Into Quarter-End
briefs.body: Veeco Instruments' 9.28% Friday advance extended a theme that has run through much of September: equipment and connectivity chip stocks outperforming broader tech. Credo Technology and Synaptics both finished in the top-six gainers, reinforcing the view that infrastructure spending around data and AI is still drawing buyers.

briefs.headline: Software-Security Sector Closes Quarter Under Pressure
briefs.body: Zscaler, Qualys, and Okta combined for losses exceeding 21 percentage points on Friday alone, dragging the Software sector to the week's worst sectoral performance at -0.82%. The cohort's struggles suggest investors are rotating proceeds from high-multiple security names into hardware and connectivity plays as quarter-end approaches.

briefs.headline: Wall Street Institutions Reassert Control of Market Direction
briefs.body: Retail participation that defined earlier phases of the 2026 rally appears to be ceding ground, with institutional flows once again emerging as the primary driver of daily price action on Wall Street. The shift could imply tighter intraday ranges and greater sensitivity to macro data releases in the weeks ahead.

briefs.headline: British Security Services Detain Five at U.S. Air Base in High-Profile Incident
briefs.body: Authorities in the United Kingdom arrested five individuals in connection with a significant security incident at a U.S. military installation, according to reports. The episode adds to a broader pattern of elevated security concerns across allied nations and may draw additional attention from defence-policy watchers as the week unfolds.
